html:
Short answer: a delegate (discussion) microphone system gives each participant a microphone unit with a talk button, while a chair unit controls who speaks. It suits boardrooms, county assemblies, council chambers and conferences where many people speak in turn and proceedings must be recorded.

When you need one

  • More than about 10 people speaking during a meeting.
  • Formal proceedings that must be recorded or streamed.
  • A chairperson who needs to control the floor.

Wired or wireless?

OptionBest for
WiredPermanent chambers and boardrooms; no batteries to manage
WirelessFlexible rooms, heritage buildings and venues where cabling is difficult

Options to consider

  • Recording and live streaming of proceedings.
  • Camera tracking that shows whoever is speaking.
  • Voting and attendance features.
  • Interpretation channels for multilingual meetings.
  • Integration with the room PA and video conferencing.

faqs.a: A delegate unit with extra controls that lets the chairperson give or remove the floor, mute all microphones and manage speaking order.

faqs.q: Can the system record meetings automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Most systems output audio for recording and streaming, and some record directly.

faqs.q: Can it work with video conferencing?
faqs.a: Yes. The delegate system can feed the room audio into Teams or Zoom so remote participants hear every speaker clearly.
